correctness.rationale: The rooted diamond bouquet has hub degree 3m, triple block I+L(P3) with eigenvalues 1,2,4 and inverse trace 7/4; grounding an endpoint or center produces rational one-/two-site block data. With hub among followers the Schur-complement identity J=sum_i tr(A_i^-1)+(1+sum_i 1ᵀA_i^-2 1)/(3m-sum_i 1ᵀA_i^-1 1) reconstructs the six exhaustive leader classes and positive denominators. The six costs are (7m-3)/4, (23m-17)/8, (59m-39)/20, (43m-39)/16, (93m-89)/36, (5m-5)/2. For m>=2 the four other nonhub values exceed center+center in different modules by respectively (3m+3)/8, (9m+11)/20, (3m+1)/16, (3m+1)/36; the hub-cost comparison is (3m-7)/4. m=1 is checked separately. Independent exact-rational inversions of every leader pair for m=1..5 establish the displayed winner counts and objectives, but the all-m claim follows from those symbolic inequalities, not numerical extrapolation. Units are unscaled Laplacian inverse trace, exactly two grounded leaders.

value.rationale: The graph is a natural repeated diamond motif in consensus networks, and the minimum total noise response under exactly two grounded nodes is a canonical control-selection statistic. A complete all-m classification identifies two sharp topological thresholds and an unexpected tie among hub-plus-every-vertex designs; a future network designer can use the precise exact rule rather than a generic optimization algorithm.
